column1: # Findings in what sheaf writes that the Arlington checker (sheaf_doc::arlington) allows, each held for a backlog entry:
# the table and key of the row the finding breaks, its rule, the corpus file it's in (* for any), the PDF version of the files
# it's allowed in, and later ones' (* for any), the entry, and why. A row any file may use must be needed by a default test
# (every_allowance_for_any_file_is_needed), a row for one corpus file by the corpus tier (just tier-arlington), and every
# entry must be an open backlog entry (every_allowance_names_an_open_backlog_entry).

column7: The model has no CA in AnnotSquare before PDF 2.0 (tsv/latest says since 2.0; its tsv/1.7 has none), though ISO 32000-1 Table 170 gives every markup annotation /CA from 1.4 and Table 169 makes Square one; AnnotCircle, Square's twin in Table 177, has it from 1.4. A model error, to report upstream.

A connector is a Link annotation, written with the keys every mark has: /CA, which a Link has only from PDF 2.0 (ISO 32000-2 Table 166), and /T and /CreationDate, which no Link has. sheaf reads its opacity back from /CA; writing it elsewhere, or raising the file to 2.0, is a design question.

sheaf's marks never raise the file's PDF version: what they write came in 1.4 (/NM, /CA, their appearances' transparency) to 1.7 (an attachment's /UF, a measurement's /Measure), and a mark on an older file leaves its version as it was. Raising it writes the catalog, a change no signature allows (M10.5 9.3). Ruled (Greg, 2026-10-24): marks raise the version when the save has no signatures to keep, in this entry's own PR; until then this row holds the finding, and after it, a mark on a signed file.

sheaf writes the standard 14 fonts it draws with (a header, a watermark, a mark's appearance) as /BaseFont alone, without /FirstChar, /LastChar, /Widths and /FontDescriptor, which PDF 2.0 asks of every simple font (ISO 32000-2 Table 109; optional for the standard 14 only before 2.0), so this row holds 2.0 files only: before 2.0, a font sheaf builds without them that isn't one of the standard 14 still fails. Writing them, always or in 2.0 files only, changes every font resource sheaf writes.

A radio field that was one object with its widget, which a save writes apart (BaseObjectsMissing), is checked as the field it is, where the file's object was checked as a widget; the model's button field tables require /DA, inheritable only, and neither the field nor the form (which has no /DA) gives one. ISO 32000-2 Table 228 asks /DA of fields with variable text, which a radio button hasn't.
